sources.title: Batch 0047 source-first inventory for UTF-8 text-file size calculation

claims.text: The source fixes five characters per record, UTF-8 encoding and 20,000,000 lines but does not preserve the actual characters, line ending or filesystem allocation semantics, so a single exact byte count is not recoverable without an explicit encoding-content assumption.

The executable Java fixture verifies 120,000,000 bytes for five ASCII code points plus LF, 320,000,000 for five common CJK code points plus LF, and 420,000,000 for five four-byte code points plus LF across 20,000,000 lines.

The fixture verifies that switching the ASCII example from LF to CRLF adds one byte per line, producing 140,000,000 bytes; the answer separately distinguishes logical byte length from filesystem allocated space.
